ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), Act No. 18467, as amended (Articles 2(2), 5(1)4 and 5-2); Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds (Act No. 17306); Commercial Act Articles 18-19; Financial Services Commission (FSC) Enforcement Decree; and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) AML/CFT supervisory regulations on beneficial ownership identification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registration Office of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public, then Apostille certificate issued by the Apostille Section, Treaty Bureau, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of the Republic of Korea via the E-Apostille online portal; this path is exclusively for Hague Apostille Convention member states. For non-member destination states, the parallel and mutually exclusive alternative is MOFA consular certification followed by legalization at the destination embassy in Seoul; Apostille and consular legalization are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Complete Corporate Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-RO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public, then Apostille by the MOFA Apostille Section via E-Apostille for Hague Apostille member states; for non-member states, the parallel route is MOFA consular certification and destination embassy legalization. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and must never be applied in sequence to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Bank Account Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial incorporators and directors of the Yuhan Hoesa (LLC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public with physical appearance of the signatories, followed by Apostille certification by MOFA for Hague Apostille member states; for non-member states, use MOFA consular certification and then legalization by the destination embassy in Seoul as an alternative path. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel options only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of Yuhan Hoesa (LLC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court of Korea (certified copy from the Court Registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified court copy notarized by a Korean notary public, followed by Apostille certification by MOFA for Hague Apostille member states; non-member states require MOFA consular certification and embassy legalization as an exclusive alternative; the two regimes are never combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank maintaining the corporate account of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued under bank seal and notarized by a Korean notary public, then certified by Apostille through MOFA for Hague Apostille member states; for non-member states, obtain MOFA consular certification and destination embassy legalization instead. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax Clearance Certificate (National Tax Completion Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), Home Tax Service portal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public followed by Apostille certification by MOFA for Hague Apostille member states; for non-member states, the parallel alternative is MOFA consular certification plus destination embassy legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, mutually exclusive paths.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders and authorized signatories against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) AML/CFT regulations, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List (required for USD Swift-wire rails), the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK OFSI consolidated sanctions, and the Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance asset-freeze designation list under the FTRA and the Proceeds of Crime Act. Daily re-screening is obligatory; enhanced due diligence includes politically exposed person (PEP) classification, source-of-wealth verification, adverse media checks, and blocking of transactions from high-risk disclosure-avoidance jurisdictions; all results must be documented in a written risk file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-RO) corporate name search and reservation module; supplementary trademark conflict screening via the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) trademark database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 18 and 19 of the Korean Commercial Act, the trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be registered in the Korean national script (Hangul). A foreign-language brand may be used in commerce only in parallel with a registered Hangul transliteration approved under the Revised Romanization of Korean rules (National Institute of Korean Language, 2000). The statutory structure follows four tiers: (1) the distinguishing brand word, (2) the industry or business specialization token, (3) the corporate form indicator 'Yuhan Hoesa' or its English equivalent 'Limited Liability Company'/'LLC', and (4) the administrative registration reference; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any pre-existing entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Korea when implying a state agency
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice issued by the competent District Court Registration Officer under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, the applicant or its legal counsel must file a written objection with the head of the same registration office within two weeks of receipt, stating the statutory basis for acceptability and rebutting the grounds of rejection. If the objection is denied, the applicant may lodge an immediate petition with the High Court appellate registration panel. In parallel, a fresh name reservation with a modified distinctive token may be filed through the i-RO portal without abandoning the appeal, ensuring operational continuity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Yuhan Hoesa must have a real registered head office in Korea (Commercial Act Article 109) and must obtain a business tax registration from the National Tax Service (NTS). For the GDP clinical logistics and freight forwarding industry (ISIC 5229), a pure virtual office, commercial mail-forwarding mailbox, or shared address without dedicated staff and operational substance is rejected by the NTS for VAT and corporate tax domicile purposes, and by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) because a Good Distribution Practice (GDP) certificate and the freight forwarding registration require physical premises with temperature-controlled storage and documented transport capacity. A serviced-office private suite with permanent signage, an occupied desk, business records, and contract files may be accepted as a registered address if economic substance can be evidenced; mailbox-only arrangements are per se impermissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) exterior signage matching the registered name; (2) physical presence of staff during municipal business hours; (3) temperature-monitoring logs and GDP standard operating procedures; (4) VAT invoices and corporate books kept at the address; (5) MFDS facility inspection before license issuance. Quantified risk: HIGH for the GDP pharma freight sector - MFDS conducts a mandatory pre-license on-site inspection (100 percent probability);

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Chapter IV, Articles 553 through 584, governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), together with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Corporate Income Tax Act as applicable to a Korean limited liability entity conducting ISIC 5229 freight transportation arrangement, customs brokerage, and pharmaceutical GDP clinical logistics support services
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea, using the Supreme Court e-Registration Internet Registration Office for electronic filing and subsequent registration extracts
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) accompanied by the notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation and all statutory attachments
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act. No statutory minimum paid-up capital, no minimum number of contributed quotas, and no blocked escrow account requirement is imposed for a Yuhan Hoesa. The total capital stated in the Articles must be subscribed by the members and paid or delivered before or on the incorporation registration date; for foreign investors the inward remittance must be evidenced by a bank certificate of foreign currency remittance or foreign currency deposit in the name of the investors, and a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act should be filed before remittance when applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). The undersigned incorporators, all members, and all persons designated as directors of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company to be organized under Articles 553 through 584 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, acting by unanimous written consent in lieu of a formal meeting, hereby record and resolve as follows: (1) Adoption of the Articles: The draft Korean-language Articles of Incorporation submitted to the meeting, including the corporate name Yuhan Hoesa, the business purpose covering ISIC 5229 international freight transportation arrangement, customs brokerage, pharmaceutical GDP clinical logistics, temperature-controlled freight validation, and all incidental services, the registered office, the total stated capital, the contribution quotas, and the governance provisions, is approved and ratified. The representative director is directed to file the approved Articles with the competent District Court Commercial Registration Division and to publish or post any notices required by law. (2) Subscription and Capital: The members' subscriptions are accepted in full, the capital of the company is fixed at the amount stated in the Articles, and each member is obligated to pay cash or deliver in-kind contributions no later than the date of registration of incorporation. Upon payment, the company shall issue contribution certificates evidencing the member's quota interests. (3) Registered Office: The registered office of the company shall be at the principal business address in the Republic of Korea set forth in the Articles and shall be within the territorial jurisdiction of the District Court in which registration is sought. No office may be moved outside the jurisdiction without amending the Articles and re-registering. (4) Banking Authorization: The representative director is authorized, solely or jointly as specified in the company's seal regulations, to open corporate bank accounts, to deposit capital and receive funds, to instruct SWIFT wire and ACH direct debit and credit transactions, to purchase and sell foreign exchange, and to execute all banking documents and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reports necessary to establish and operate the company's payment rails. (5) Appointment of Officers: The following statutory officers are appointed: representative director, the directors named in the written consents, and the auditor, if required by law or the Articles. Each appointee accepts office and undertakes to exercise the duty of care of a good manager under the Commercial Act, to maintain corporate books and records, to register the corporate seal, and to cause the company to obtain the National Tax Service business registration certificate and all applicable pharmaceutical GDP and civil defense licenses before commencing regulated operations. (6) Execution: Each director and authorized counsel may execute, sign, notarize, apostille, and deliver all documents and pay all fees required to complete the incorporation, to open bank accounts, and to effect the first board resolution. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability review and pre-registration of foreign investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, Court Registration Information Office through the e-Registration Internet Registration Office; for foreign investment, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the KOTRA One-Stop Foreign Investment Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability review against the commercial registry database to confirm that the proposed corporate name Yuhan Hoesa and its corresponding Korean registration name do not conflict with an existing trade name. Determine whether any shareholder is a non-resident or foreign legal entity; if so, prepare and file an advance foreign investment report before the capital remittance through KOTRA or the Foreign Investment Information System. The report must identify the foreign investor, the amount, and the proposed use of funds. If the business is a freight arrangement and pharmaceutical logistics validation company with no physical factory, no manufacturing license pre-approval is required at this stage. Retain the report receipt because it will be submitted with the court incorporation registration later.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in Korean and English
Passport or corporate documents of each member
Foreign investment report form if applicable
Power of attorney for the local filing agent
Certificate of seal impression or authenticated corporate resolution of each corporate investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search shows identity or unfair similarity with an existing registered name, select a new distinctive Korean name and amend all associated formation documents before filing. If the foreign investment report is suspended, respond to the MOTIE or KOTRA document supplementation notice within the statutory period and re-submit the corrected report receipt before continuing to capital remittance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public commissioned by the Supreme Court of Korea through the Korean Notary Association at the place of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in accordance with Commercial Act Articles 553 through 584. The Articles must expressly contain the company name, business purposes covering ISIC 5229 freight forwarding, customs brokerage, GDP-compliant pharmaceutical distribution logistics, clinical product freight validation, and all legally incidental activities, the principal registered office, total stated capital, contributed quota amounts and values, number of directors, representation method, auditor provisions, calling and termination rules, and liquidation provisions. Submit the completed draft to a notary public for certification of the signatures and seals of all incorporators. If any incorporator is outside the Republic of Korea, the power of attorney must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and apostilled or consularized as needed. The notarial certificate is an indispensable legal prerequisite for the subsequent court registration and must be obtained before any capital verification or registration filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the founding members meeting
Notarized power of attorney and corporate resolutions for non-resident members
Passport copies and seal certificates of all incorporators
Written consent to appointment of directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires substantive corrections, prepare a clean revised draft, obtain unanimous approval from all members, and execute the corrected Articles. If a foreign power of attorney lacks apostille or consular legalization, cure the authentication deficiency and resubmit the revised package to the notary before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea authorized to handle foreign exchange under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with information transmitted to the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary deposit account or use an authorized inward remittance facility designated for the incorporation so that the capital contributions stated in the Articles are paid in cash or delivered in kind. For foreign shareholders, the contributed amount must be received as a foreign currency inward remittance evidenced by a bank certificate of inward remittance or a certificate of foreign currency deposit. The bank shall issue a capital contribution verification certificate when the contributions are actually paid by the members. No blocked escrow account is required under Korean law for a Yuhan Hoesa, but the foreign investment report receipt must be matched with the bank receipt to prove the lawful arrival of foreign capital. The verification certificate and remittance certificates must be retained for the court registration application.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank account opening forms for the temporary contribution account
Inward remittance instruction and bank receipt
Certificate of inward foreign currency remittance or foreign currency deposit
Capital contribution schedule showing each member's quota and payment date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If remittance is delayed, update the contribution schedule and if necessary reduce the stated capital by a formal members' resolution before signing amended Articles. If the bank asks for a revised foreign investment declaration, cooperate with the bank to file a supplementary foreign exchange report and obtain a corrected inward remittance certificate before filing for incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration of incorporation at the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Section of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, using the Supreme Court e-Registration Internet Registration Office for electronic case filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company together with the notarized Articles, the capital contribution verification certificate, proof of the registered office such as a lease agreement with landlord consent, and the written acceptances of the representative director, directors, and auditor. Pay the registration tax, education surtax, and court filing fees through the court treasury or electronic payment system. The court performs a formal legality review and does not evaluate commercial viability. After acceptance, the court issues a certified certificate of registration, and the company legally comes into existence on the registration date. After the court registration, request a certified corporate registration abstract and prepare to apply for the National Tax Service business registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a limited liability company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital contribution verification certificate issued by the bank
Landlord written consent and lease copy for the registered office
Written acceptance of the representative director, directors, and auditor
Foreign investment report receipt if applicable
Power of attorney for the local registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure the omitted item within the time stated in the order, normally five business days, and pay any additional duty. If registration is suspended because of a name conflict or pending foreign investment matter, remove the blocking cause, submit the corrected documents, and pay the applicable refiling fee to complete registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service business registration and statutory insurance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service local district tax office, Business Registration Division, through the HomeTax electronic portal; National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and local Employment and Labor Office for mandatory social insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After court registration, file for the corporate business registration certificate under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. Provide the corporate taxpayer data including the legal entity name, representative director, registered office, business purpose, and accounting period, and request corporate electronic tax invoice issuance. Enroll the representative director, employees, and working officers in the four major Korean social insurance programs as required by the National Pension Act, National Health Insurance Act, Employment Insurance Act, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act. The business registration certificate does not authorize GDP pharmaceutical logistics but serves as the foundational tax license and as a prerequisite for opening a fully activated corporate bank account and for applying for operational licenses with the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration issued by the court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease or ownership documents
Corporate seal certificate
Representative director identification
Corporate bank account confirmation if already opened
Director appointment records and officer consent letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office sends a document deficiency notice, provide the missing identity, lease, or corporate registration evidence through HomeTax within the statutory response period, normally 10 days. If the tax office asserts incorrect jurisdictional allocation, request the correct district tax office to accept the file or appeal the allocation through the National Tax Service internal review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance execution, bank activation, and GDP compliance kickoff
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank for SWIFT wire and direct ACH payment rails; Ministry of Food and Drug Safety regional pharmaceutical safety office for GDP and pharmaceutical logistics permits; local fire safety authority and Ministry of Employment and Labor for workplace and civil defense clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the formal First Board Resolution and open the operating corporate account and foreign currency account, activate the SWIFT and ACH payment rails, set internal payment limits, and adopt a corporate seal usage policy. Prepare the pharmaceutical Good Distribution Practice quality manual, cold chain temperature excursion procedure, storage and distribution SOPs, batch freight documentation, adverse event reporting, product recall protocol, and staff training plan for clinical trial product logistics. If the company operates a physical storage or distribution site, submit the MFDS pharmaceutical logistics authorization application and obtain fire safety and occupational safety certificates before receiving inventory. If the company operates only as a certified freight arrangement and validation intermediary, issue a written scope determination confirming that all physical storage is delegated to MFDS-licensed GDP warehouses and retain the contractual chain evidencing that compliance.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes
Business registration certificate
Corporate registration abstract
Bank account application and AML/KYC dossier
GDP quality manual and distribution validation master plan
MFDS application forms and facility floor plan if storage is operated
Civil defense fire safety certificate
Occupational health and safety risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS questions the scope of GDP authorization, submit a written scope confirmation and the contractual chain showing that each physical warehouse is licensed and compliant. If fire safety clearance is deferred, remediate the cited fire protection defects, request a re-inspection, and suspend pharmaceutical storage operations until the certificate is reinstated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety Regional Pharmaceutical Safety Bureau; local fire safety authority under the National Fire Agency; Ministry

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity (Yuhan Hoesa) undertaking economic activity in South Korea: 1) Appoint a domestic tax representative 'Witakin' having physical presence in Korea, unless the foreign entity is deemed to have a permanent establishment or a place of business; 2) File the 'Application for Business Registration for Foreign Corporation' (Form no. 4 of the Value-Added Tax Act enforcement rules) with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the tax representative's address or the place of business; 3) Submit incorporation certificate, foreign registration certificate or equivalent notarized and apostilled corporate existence evidence, plus a power of attorney designating the tax representative; 4) Upon acceptance, the NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (Saeupja Deungrokbeonho), which simultaneously serves as the VAT registration number and mandatory corporate tax file reference; 5) If the foreign entity has no Korean business establishment, register independently as a 'non-resident place of business' using an end-dated provisional ID; the required application must be lodged before beginning taxable supplies, and for importing goods an importer bond or customs registration via UNI-PASS is also required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - the Republic of Korea does not adopt US-style check-the-box elections. A company formed as a limited liability 'Yuhan Hoesa' is automatically taxed as a corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and no hybrid mismatch election is available for outbound payments except for routine anti-deferral and controlled foreign corporation rules. Foreign corporations may elect the 'domestic business place' filing regime under Article 94 of the Corporate Income Tax Act when they meet the domestic source income threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for non-resident suppliers. Any business that makes taxable supplies of goods or services in Korea, including via cross-border electronic or digital services, must register with the NTS regardless of turnover. For domestic small businesses with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000, a simplified taxpayer filing regime applies, but simplified taxpayers are still mandatorily issued a VAT Business Registration Number and must periodically file a simplified VAT return. Non-resident suppliers are subject to irreversible registration without a turnover relief threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-invoice) issuance through HomeTax, with real-time data transmission to the NTS under the 'Electronic Tax Invoice Mandatory Issuance System'. Since 2023, e-invoices are compulsory for all B2B transactions where the total invoice value exceeds KRW 100,000, and for B2C transactions regarding simplified tax invoices; issuance must be transmitted to the NTS within 3 days after the supply tax point (day after the statutory invoice date for daily aggregation). Failure to transmit falsifies the claim base. The system requires API integration or the HomeTax batch upload portal, and all invoices must contain an electronic serial number (codeferred by NTS), the VAT payer's registration number, recipient's registration number, date, item description, net amount, VAT amount and grand total. No separate cryptographic fiscal stamping exists, but NTS data validation is automated and anti-fraud matching uses cross-referencing between customs (UNI-PASS) filings, bank remittance evidence and e-invoice data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act Article 0.0 (Zero-rating of exported goods and services), exports of all tangible goods are zero-rated when: (a) the goods are shipped or transported out of the Republic of Korea within the statutory export period; (b) the export is evidenced by a Customs Export Declaration (수출신고필증) issued under the Customs Act; (c) title and risk have passed to a non-resident purchaser; and (d) the foreign exchange has been received in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Additionally, qualifying offshore digital services (e.g., B2B digital services performed entirely outside Korea) may be zero-rated if the recipient is a non-resident business, the service is supplied to a foreign territory and the NTS Foreign Exchange Transaction Certificate shows inward remittance from abroad. The claim must be supported by standard export documentary evidence and made in the quarterly VAT return. For goods, the zero rate applies both to outright exports and to sales of goods to be delivered in Korea but then moved abroad under customs supervision (bonded export transactions).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate / 수출신고필증) issued by the Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS)
Original or electronic commercial invoice with the statutory zero-rating indication
Bill of Lading (for sea shipments) or Airway Bill (for air shipments) showing the Korean exporter and foreign consignee
Packing list and certificate of origin where required
Supplier's VAT registration certificate and tax representative appointment deed for any third-party handlers (e.g., GDP freight forwarder)

Proof of foreign exchange repatriation either via the institutionally designated foreign exchange bank's 'Import/Export Exchange Payment Confirmation' (수출대금 입금증명) or a Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation Certificate
Freight forwarding contract and customs broker power of attorney evidencing physical outbound logistics for pharmaceutical GDP cold chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS retail VAT audit unit and Korea Customs Service jointly inspect export zero-rating claims. If documentary evidence (particularly the Export Declaration Certificate and foreign exchange remittance certificate) is fraudulent, incomplete, or the goods are later found not to have physically left Korea, the NTS will assess the full 10% VAT on the export value (denying the zero rate) and impose an additional 10% of the assessed tax as an administrative fine under the Framework Act on National Taxes (equivalent to under-reporting penalties). If the false claim is deemed tax evasion ('severe negligence' or 'fraudulent evasion'), a penalty of 40% of the unpaid tax may be imposed, plus a 20% overdue charge for unpaid periods. Criminal prosecution under Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can lead to imprisonment not exceeding 2 years or a fine not exceeding two times the evaded amount. Furthermore, the NTS will claw back any previously refunded input VAT directly attributable to the erroneous zero-rated exports, and the tax representative becomes jointly liable for the unpaid VAT, penalties and interest. For pharmaceutical GDP logistics, additional regulatory sanctions under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act (suspension of the GDP license) may be triggered if the export documentation falsification also violates the Good Distribution Practice certification requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, exercised jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MoEF) and the Korea Customs Service as the statutory foreign-exchange control apparatus of South Korea.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized, largely market-determined foreign exchange regime, managed not by exchange controls but by a reporting and verification framework. Current-account transactions, such as export/import settlements, freight and logistics fees, royalties, and ordinary service payments, are freely convertible through designated foreign exchange banks after the submitting entity provides a proper transaction classification and evidential documents; no prior central-bank consent is normally required. Capital-account transactions, however, are subject to a stricter architecture. An inbound equity subscription to a Korean limited liability company is a foreign-direct-investment capital transaction that must be reported or approved under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; the funds must be remitted by the identified shareholder and received into a Korean bank account in the name of the resident entity. Profit remittances are legally current-account-like but are treated as current-account transactions requiring strict verification: the bank requires audited financial statements, shareholder and board resolutions, tax clearance certificates, and proof of distributable retained earnings, and the remittance may be stopped where dividend documentation is incomplete. Export proceeds are not subject to a mandatory surrender ratio; the exporter may keep the foreign currency in a foreign-currency account or convert it at market rate. The practical convertibility hurdles are therefore not formal restrictions but customer due diligence, transaction code accuracy, economic-purpose validation, and the de facto in-person KYC requirements for foreign directors and shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, there is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the Bank of Korea and no fixed conversion ratio to KRW. Exporters must obtain payment through one of the accepted settlement methods in the underlying contract (advance payment, sight L/C, usance L/C, D/P, D/A, or open account). For ordinary pharma freight and logistics services, the standard statutory collection expectation is that the full invoice payment is received within 90 days from the date of export declaration or service completion; a longer collection window may be declared and approved for project-type contracts or capital goods with deferred payment terms, but the complete proceeds must be repatriated by the confirmed deadline and either credited to the selling entity's domestic foreign-currency account or converted to KRW at the market rate. Any overdue non-collection must be explained to the designated foreign exchange bank and the Korea Customs Service, with enforcement reflected in the entity's trade statistics and compliance profile.

Basic Operational Currency Account; Foreign Currency Trade Settlement Account

Capital Escrow Account; Basic Operational Currency Account; Clearing Account for SWIFT MT103

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for entity domiciliation and primary treasury. Offshore digital EMIs are not licensed by the Financial Services Commission nor registered as designated foreign-exchange businesses to hold KRW or execute Korean payments; they cannot provide local corporate bank accounts, IBANs, or permitted capital-verification evidence. They may only be used as an ancillary non-KRW expense channel for small operational payments to foreign suppliers where the EMI is fully licensed in its home jurisdiction. All equity injections, export collections, tax payments, and outbound trade settlements must flow through a domestic designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Using an EMI as the main operating bank would trigger automatic compliance rejection and may invalidate capital verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is mandatory for the statutory director(s), the beneficial owner(s), and any signatories during initial corporate onboarding. Korean Tier-1 banks generally do not allow remote or consular proxy opening for a newly formed foreign-owned Korean LLC. If the foreign director cannot travel, the entity must, at a minimum: appoint a resident Korean representative with a notarized and apostilled power of attorney; have every foreign signatory's passport and corporate authority documents apostilled and translated into Korean; and complete a scheduled live video-call compliance interview with bank AML officers. Some banks may, at their sole discretion, permit a proxy to complete the paperwork, but the bank compliance officer will still require direct video identification of the natural-person UBO. In practice, KYC risk scoring for a pharma logistics entity is standard, but the no-show of a director is the number-one reason onboarding is refused.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO transparency deficiency: nominee layers, wide member registry, or beneficial owners hidden by a foreign trust structure trigger Korean beneficial-ownership registration duties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the notarized Korean-language articles of incorporation, English/Korean shareholder register, apostilled UBO declaration signed by all natural persons holding 25% or more of the LLC, certified passport copies of each UBO, source of funds letter, and a written corporate chain diagram from the Yuhan Hoesa up to the ultimate natural persons, together with the non-resident investment registration or exemption certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and restricted-party exposure in GDP pharma freight: proposed counterparties, carrier, ports, or consolidators may touch DPRK, OFAC, EU, or UNSC-listed economies or persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete counterparty and end-user list, bank screening agreement, OFAC- and UNSC-style denied-party screening reports for all counterparties, shipping vessel and route detail, airway or bill of lading, cargo value and Incoterms schedule, customs export or import declarations, and the approved GDP logistics contract proving the goods are time/temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical products and not dual-use or controlled items.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering in pharma freight: over-invoiced or under-invoiced GDP logistics services, duplicate invoices, or mismatch between goods description and remittance reason.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the signed original service agreement, item-by-item invoice with ISIC 5229 scope and unit economics, temperature-logged warehouse receipts and CMR/airway bills, GPS handover records, proof-of-delivery signatures, customs declarations referencing the pharmaceutical cargo, a self-monitored transaction flowchart, and audited cost-support schedules that reconcile each disbursement to a physical logistics movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of starting capital or third-party loan funding: inbound wire amounts inconsistent with the stated share capital, tax residency mismatch, or value passing through unregulated money remitters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble the complete funding file: remitting shareholder's bank statements covering the preceding 6 months, signed equity or shareholder-loan agreement, board resolution for capital contribution, business plan and valuation basis, proof of tax residence of each remitter, a no-cryptocurrency/no-informal-value-transfer declaration, and the capital verification certificate to be stamped by the receiving designated foreign exchange bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound equity wire must be sent by the actual shareholder identified in the Korean LLC's articles and foreign-investment notification; third-party payment is prohibited. The funds should be routed via SWIFT through the remitter's home bank to the Korean entity's capital escrow account at a designated foreign exchange bank. On the wire, the remitter must include the Korean foreign-exchange transaction purpose classification for equity subscription/investment, the name of the target Korean entity, and the investment registration or notification number where required. The receiving bank will match the wire, remitter name, amount, and purpose code against the board resolution and investment report before crediting. For KRW conversion, the bank applies the market rate and issues a foreign-currency deposit receipt or paid-in capital confirmation containing value date, transaction code, amount, and beneficiary, which auditors use for capital verification. Any deviation from the registered investor name or purpose code will freeze the funds pending AML review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Pharmaceutical GDP freight payments should be pushed overseas using SWIFT MT103 for bank-to-bank correspondent wires; this is the preferred rail because each transfer carries a structured purpose code and full sender/receiver details, thereby satisfying Korean designated-bank due diligence. For purchase of pharmaceutical precursors or temperature-controlled cargo, the bank may issue an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (L/C) under UCP600 if the overseas principal requires payment certainty; the L/C goods description must exactly match the import declaration and GDP documentation. For lower-value recurring freight, taxis and documentary collections (D/P) are viable but slower. Domestic KRW vendor payments, fuel, lease, and payroll are paid through the local ACH-like interbank transfer using the bank's electronic payment platform. All wire outs must be pre-flagged with supporting contract, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airway bill, and customs entry.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts with a designated Korean bank, covering the exact invoice or expected cash-flow amount in the underlying trade, freight, or equity transaction, usually limited to 12 months and requiring under-documentation.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) transactions through authorized domestic banks or approved international branches, used only where the offshore counterparty cannot receive KRW delivery or where the hedge amount matches a committed foreign-currency exposure; speculative uncovered NDFs are prohibited.

Cross-currency swaps and simple collar structures subject to mandatory bank conformity with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the swap tenor must not exceed the underlying loan or equity subscription maturity, and the transaction cannot be entered before the bank has verified the real foreign-currency balance sheet exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Return and Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax; Local Tax Officer of the registered head-office municipality for the surtax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file adds 20% of the unpaid corporate tax (30% for fraudulent omission); under-reporting adds 10% (20% for fraudulent under-reporting). Delinquency interest accrues at 0.03% per day (annualized 11.0%) until full payment. Continued non-payment triggers forced collection, asset seizure, criminal referral for tax evasion, cancellation of business registration by the NTS, and ultimately administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Preliminary Corporate Income Tax Return (Interim Prepayment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the first six months of the fiscal year; for calendar-year entities, by August 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the preliminary return triggers an additional tax of 20% on the omitted or under-reported amount plus daily delinquency interest at 0.03%. Repeated non-compliance may result in deemed tax assessment, compulsory enforcement, and cancellation of the business registration certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Final Returns for the First and Second Half-Year Tax Periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax e-VAT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (January 1 to June 30) due by July 25; second half (July 1 to December 31) due by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 5% additional tax applies for failure to file the final VAT return; underpaid VAT accrues daily delinquency interest at 0.03%. Omitted tax invoices expose the entity to penalties of 2% of the undeclared supply value and, for fraudulent evasion, potential criminal prosecution and registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Preliminary (Interim) Returns for the First and Second Quarters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax e-VAT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First preliminary return (January to March) due April 25; second preliminary return (July to September) due October 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a preliminary VAT return triggers a 2% surcharge on the unpaid VAT, plus daily delinquency interest at 0.03%. Persistent non-filing may lead to deemed assessments, seizure of receivables or bank accounts, and eventual business-registration strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Enterprise Status Report and Business Operation Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the close of the business year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit may result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,500), loss of foreign-investment tax relief or subsidy eligibility, and impediments to dividend remittance. Continued non-compliance may lead to cancellation of foreign-investment registration and administrative corrective orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Independent Auditor's Report (if subject to mandatory external audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year end; where the auditor is engaged, audited financial statements must be filed with the FSS within two weeks after the members' meeting adopting the statements, and in any event no later than the statutory audit-filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Companies may trigger correction orders from the Financial Services Commission, administrative fines up to KRW 70 million, designation of a forced auditor, suspension of tax incentives, criminal fines or imprisonment for directors, and civil liability for losses arising from un-audited or defective statements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Korea's Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Companies (as amended, effective for fiscal years beginning on or after May 1, 2019), an independent CPA audit is mandatory for: (a) any company, including a Yuhan Hoesa LLC, whose total assets at fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million); (b) any non-listed company meeting any two of the following: (i) total assets of at least KRW 10 billion, (ii) total liabilities of at least KRW 5 billion, (iii) annual turnover of at least KRW 10 billion, (iv) an average of at least 100 regular employees; and (c) all listed companies (KOSPI, KOSDAQ, or KONEX). The Financial Services Commission may also designate a company for external audit on public-interest or shareholder-protection grounds. For pharmaceutical GDP freight operations, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) may require an independent audit of GDP compliance, inventory traceability, and approved logistics records even when asset/turnover thresholds are not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to listed companies and companies mandated to use K-IFRS. For non-public entities subject to a statutory audit or preparing local statutory financial statements, Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) are permitted, with the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SAS for SMEs) available for eligible smaller LLCs. GDP pharmaceutical freight operations must additionally maintain MFDS-prescribed batch tracking, cold-chain integrity logs, and distribution records consistent with the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act and Good Distribution Practice requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a standalone public UBO register for domestic non-listed LLCs. The Yuhan Hoesa must, however, maintain an updated members' register at its registered office and record every member transfer promptly. Foreign investors holding 10% or more of equity must file an annual foreign-invested enterprise status report with MOTIE/KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank by March 31 of each year; any transfer or change in foreign beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the event. For AML/CFT purposes, customer due diligence and beneficial-owner identification data must be refreshed at least annually or upon any triggering event, particularly because the entity receives freight payments through Swift Wire and Direct ACH rails.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Officers
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Security Interests
Minute Book of General Meetings and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per year (inclusive of registered office, Korean-language statutory secretarial service, and compliance mail forwarding)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 32,000 per year (standalone or consolidated audited financial statements, including GDP inventory verification, cold-chain traceability review, and confirmation of freight receivables)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% national CIT on first KRW 200,000,000 taxable income; 19% above KRW 200,000,000; 21% above KRW 20,000,000,000; 24% above KRW 300,000,000,000, plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national CIT, producing a 9.9% aggregate rate on the first bracket
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general Korean free-zone CIT holiday after BEPS reforms; applicable incentives include the R&D tax credit for qualified cold-chain or GDP logistics technology, foreign investment tax credit in Free Economic Zones, and temporary investment, employment, or facility credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act. Income from ISIC 5229 GDP pharma freight is normally taxable unless a specific statutory exemption applies; patent-box treatment is not a separate Korean regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return, Form 5 for domestic corporations, filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal; financial statements and attached statutory tax schedules are submitted simultaneously.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final corporate income tax return with semi-annual preliminary corporate tax payments during the business year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; one additional month may be approved by the district tax office where independent audited financial statements are pending; non-resident stamp or tax representative filings are subject to the same deadline absent a specific extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, taxpayer registration number, fiscal year-end, jurisdiction of incorporation, registered address, and industry code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that KR_YUHANGHOESA is a Korean domestic corporation liable to Korean CIT on worldwide income; enter country code of ultimate foreign shareholder and disclose percentage ownership; attach beneficial ownership and registered owner information for non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from freight forwarding, GDP storage and distribution, delivery management, client reimbursable expenses, and other operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Korea-source GDP freight service revenue on accrual basis; convert foreign-currency revenue at the exchange rate applicable on the transaction date or average rate approved by the Korean tax authority; do not net intercompany freight charges or pass-through disbursements without supporting contracts and evidence of economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and cost of services, including direct GDP logistics labour, warehouse rental, cold-chain utilities, qualified-person salaries, transportation subcontracts, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only costs supported by invoice, payment proof, and entered into with independent-parties arm’s-length pricing; where costs are paid to a non-resident related party, attach transfer pricing documentation proving comparable third-party rates for pharma GDP transport and cold-chain storage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general and administrative expenses, including management fees, IT systems, insurance, professional fees, royalties, interest, and travel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany royalties and management charges must pass the beneficial ownership and economic substance test; expenses paid to a non-resident related party may be disallowed if Korea-source activity is not actually performed in Korea or if the payer is only a mailbox entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and statutory adjustments: entertainment in excess of limits, fines, donations exceeding deduction limits, corporate taxes, unsubstantiated cash freight expenses, and domestic related-party transaction costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back penalties, imported-pharma customs fines, taxes treated as withheld irrecoverable amounts, and inflated management fees paid to non-residents; failure to add back generates the 20% unfaithful return penalty and allows Korean tax authorities to pierce the corporate veil.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special related-party transaction schedule and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all cross-border related-party revenue and expense transactions by type, entity, country, and methodology; if aggregate related-party transactions exceed the statutory threshold, attach Local File and Master File on the NTS portal; use approved arm’s length methods and disclose any prior Yearly Compliance Assessment adjustment or mutual agreement procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of taxable income: gross income less costs, expenses, non-taxable income, deductions, and carryforward tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled entities may deduct tax loss carryforwards only if the return was filed timely; hidden profit distributions disguised as deductible payments are recharacterized as dividends subject to withholding tax and penalty additions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credit adjustments, including foreign tax credits, corporate structure conversion credits, employment credits, and R&D credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits may reduce Korean CIT only where the domestic entity has direct ownership of the cash-generating GDP operation; a non-resident shareholder cannot claim personal tax credits on the Korean corporate return. Supported by field-by-field evidence where the real beneficial owner is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax before surtax using the progressive statutory CIT rates on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9/19/21/24 per-cent progressive brackets before the 10% local income tax surtax; the effective combined rate on the first KRW 200 million taxable income is 9.9%; non-resident owners should model both national and local rates because local surtax is not treaty-exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions for reductions from tax treaty automatic exemption, tax credits, preliminary taxes paid, and taxes withheld by payers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Subtract Korean preliminary corporate tax payments and any withholding taxes already borne by the domestic entity; do not subtract income tax of the non-resident parent unless a valid foreign tax credit or treaty pass-through mechanism applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Surtax computation: local income tax at 10% of the computed national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Even if the non-resident parent is treaty-protected, the Korean local income tax surtax computed on the corporate return must be paid; the domestic company is responsible for the surtax and cannot shift it to the non-resident shareholder unless contractually allocated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate tax payable, refund, or carryforward after installments and creditable preliminary taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Set out intercompany tax reconciliations with non-resident shareholders; attach evidence of prepayments and any approved treaty refunds for dividend, interest, or royalty over-withholding before the statutory deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure schedule for non-resident dividend, interest, royalty, and CIGA information, beneficial ownership, economic substance, and country-by-country obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify each non-resident shareholder’s tax residence, whether the Tax Residency Certificate is attached, percentage of ownership, treaty articles relied on, expected outbound withholding rates, and whether the Korean Yuhan Hoesa has core income-generating activities in Korea.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and non-payment: an addition to tax equal to 20% of the unpaid national CIT, plus daily delinquency interest of 0.022% from the original due date. Underreported or omitted tax attributable to concealment or false invoices triggers an additional 40% fraudulent omission penalty under the Framework Act on Taxation; false tax invoices carry separate penalties under the VAT Act and Act on the Punishment of Tax Offenses. Criminal tax fraud on amounts exceeding KRW 500,000,000 can rise to aggravated imprisonment up to 10 years, with fines up to 5 times the defrauded tax and prohibition from departure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on gross dividends paid to non-residents, plus 10% local income tax surtax on the withholding amount, giving an aggregate statutory rate of 22%; a Double Tax Treaty may reduce the rate to 5-15% depending on shareholding and treaty terms.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean payer must withhold 22% unless the non-resident beneficial owner files an Application for Income Tax Reduction or Exemption under a Tax Agreement with the National Tax Service before payment; attach a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence-country competent authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, corporate documentation showing CIGA, and LOB substantiation. If the treaty claim is not made before payment, the beneficiary may apply for refund by filing an amended or rectifying withholding declaration within 3 years from the statutory filing date; Korean authorities may request exchange of information from the treaty partner before granting relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest and royalties to non-residents is also 20% national plus 10% local surtax, or 22% aggregate. Typical Korean DTA rates are 10-15% on interest and 5-15% on royalties; royalties for industrial, scientific, or cold-chain logistics technology are generally assessable under Article 12 of the OECD-Korea treaty and require beneficial ownership. Intercompany interest must reflect arm’s length rate and cannot exceed statutory thin-capitalization limits or interest deduction limits under Korean tax law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions during the business year when total revenue is at least KRW 100,000,000,000 triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; Country-by-Country Report is required when the consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds KRW 1,000,000,000,000; every related-party transaction exceeding KRW 50,000,000 must be disclosed on the NTS intercompany transaction schedule.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but Framework Act on Taxation Article 14 requires substance-over-form; a KR_YUHANGHOESA entity with no physical GDP freighting functions, no qualified-person employment, no freight contract risk, and no decision-making authority in Korea will be treated as a sham for Korean tax purposes. Core Income-Generating Activities for ISIC 5229 GDP pharma freight include Korean GDP licensed warehouse operations, cold-chain quality assurance, local invoicing, pharmaceutical distribution contracts, inventory risk, and strategic management exercised by local directors, all of which must be documented for treaty and transfer pricing purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion through Inflated Intercompany Logistics Costs
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing the annual Korean CIT return using inflated freight, cold-chain storage, or handling charges invoiced by a related non-resident logistics entity without arm’s length benchmarking, without performance of real CIGA by that entity, and with false or backdated transport waybills to shift profit from Korea to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reclassification of the excess payment as a disguised dividend or non-deductible expense; restoration of taxable income; 20% understatement penalty plus 0.022% daily delinquency interest; an additional 40% omission penalty for fraudulent concealment; criminal liability under the Act on the Punishment of Tax Offenses with imprisonment up to 3 years and fines up to 5 times the evaded tax, or up to 10 years for amounts exceeding KRW 500,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where directors authorized false invoices or knowingly created a nominal related provider; directors can be personally and jointly liable for unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and delinquency interest; travel bans, blacklisting by the NTS, asset seizure, forfeiture of improperly transferred freight receipts, and imprisonment are available sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and DTA Relief Abuse for Non-Resident Profit Extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a no-substance offshore intermediate corporation to own shares of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, with the offshore entity having no office, employees, books, or operational functions, merely to claim treaty dividend withholding rate at 10% or less and then divert the dividend to a shareholder in a non-treaty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits; withholding at the full 22% statutory rate plus 20% failure-to-withhold penalty; immediate recapture of the underwithheld tax; rejection of the tax loss carryforward where the return is deemed sham; Article 14 of the Framework Act on Taxation disregards the intermediate company and levies 40% fraudulent omission additions on the disguised distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false beneficial ownership statements, produce false minutes, or place assets beyond creditor reach face civil joint liability for the entire tax deficiency; NTS departure blacklisting and seizure of personal assets may occur; criminal provisions apply for assisting a sham structure designed to defeat Korean withholding tax with imprisonment up to 10 years in aggravated fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Tax Invoice and AML Facilitation Using GDP Freight Front
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing legally valid Korean tax invoices for pharmaceutical freight and logistics services that were never physically performed, or accepting payments through Swift Wire or Direct ACH from unidentified beneficial owners connected to unregistered or smuggled good-distribution-practice cargo, thereby laundering disguised fees, evading import UD customs valuation, and facilitating subsidiary VAT fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT addition to tax of 20% of the false invoice amount and criminal fine up to 3 times of the abusively reported supply value; customs penalties under the Customs Act for unlicensed pharmaceutical entry; Ministry of Food and Drug Safety license revocation for GDP pharmacy logistics; Act on the Punishment of Tax Offenses provides imprisonment up to 3 years for false invoice issue; AML fines and administrative orders from the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit may also attach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual directors and officers can be separately charged with fraudulent tax invoice issuance and money laundering facilitation, including personal asset forfeiture based on freight payments traced through their bank IDs; civil piercing extends to directors who signed the false waybills, approved the wire, or bore personal benefit, resulting in unlimited joint liability in addition to criminal imprisonment up to 10 years under aggravated economic crime treatment.
